data.title: PostgreSQL
data.tagline: An open-source database management system that stores and queries related data in tables
data.learningOutcome: Distinguish database software from SQL instructions and verify a relationship using valid and invalid user IDs.
data.description: For example, store users and orders in separate tables and require each order to reference an existing user. PostgreSQL can enforce that constraint, but the rule must be configured; installation alone does not define your business rules.

learning.assumes: Know that users and orders can be stored as records.
learning.outcome: Distinguish database software from SQL instructions and verify a relationship using valid and invalid user IDs.

distinctions.label: Database
distinctions.explanation: A Database contains organized data; PostgreSQL is one software system used to manage databases.

distinctions.label: SQL
distinctions.explanation: SQL is the instruction language; PostgreSQL executes those instructions and manages the stored data.

explanation.title: Software, data and instructions
explanation.text: A Database stores organized data; PostgreSQL is the software managing it; SQL is the language used to query, write and define constraints. The backend executes instructions through a database connection and the page displays the result.

explanation.title: Configure rules for the business
explanation.text: A foreign key checks whether the referenced user exists. Use a Transaction separately when order creation and stock deduction must commit together. A valid reference does not grant access; the backend still checks ownership and permission.

explanation.title: Separate built-in features from extensions
explanation.text: PostgreSQL supports tables, indexes and JSON queries. Vector similarity search can be provided by extensions such as pgvector, which must be installed or enabled by the host and are not present in every instance by default.

data.boundary: Database constraints enforce only the rules you define. Access controls, backups and recovery still need configuration, and a database transaction does not automatically reverse an external payment.

lessonPractice.title: The page lists only existing users, but other programs also write orders. How can invalid user references be prevented?

options.label: Configure a foreign key so the database checks each order write
options.feedback: Every write path must satisfy the reference rule; nonexistent user IDs are rejected.

options.label: Keep only the page’s user dropdown synchronized with current users
options.feedback: Page options cannot constrain writes made by other programs.

options.label: Periodically find orders with missing users and clean them up
options.feedback: Invalid orders exist until cleanup; this does not enforce the relationship on each write.

data.agentPrompt: Store users and orders in PostgreSQL and add a foreign key for each order’s user ID. Try existing and nonexistent user IDs; verify that the first saves and the second is rejected without leaving an order.
